idiom_name: enum with associated values plus Codable init(from:) switching on the discriminator key
implementation_notes: The canonical message is a Swift enum with associated values, so every downstream switch is exhaustive by compiler rule, and Codable does the routing: a custom init(from:) reads the discriminator from a CodingKey container and switches to the matching case, where each case decodes its own payload through the per-format translator; JSONDecoder and DecodingError.dataCorruptedError provide the wire plumbing and the natural unknown-format path. A protocol (a WireFormatDecoding with registered conformers) remains justified when translators must be injected with a client or code tables, and hand-written mapping is unavoidable for non-JSON sources such as CSV or fixed width, because Codable describes keyed and unkeyed containers rather than arbitrary grammars.
pitfalls: try? or catch { nil } turns a decoding failure into a silently skipped message; propagate DecodingError so the invalid-message channel sees the offending key and payload.
JSONDecoder.dateDecodingStrategy defaults to .deferredToDate (seconds since 2001), so partner dates need an explicit ISO-8601 strategy before the canonical form is trustworthy.
Money decoded as Double loses precision - decode into Decimal and keep the scale, or the canonical amount differs from the source.
keyDecodingStrategy = .convertFromSnakeCase makes keys that differ only by an underscore collide (user_id and userId), which is a real hazard when one decoder absorbs several partners' spellings.
